A report names only the site you report from; other pages appear as “page 1”, “page 2” and their links are removed. Entries older than seven days are deleted. The log stays on this computer and is never sent anywhere until you choose to open an issue with it — and nothing is submitted until you press GitHub's own button.

walkthrough.article.recognised.text.message: No pill on a reference means ORE could not identify it, so nothing was checked for it.

walkthrough.article.recognised.title.message: A pill means ORE recognised the paper

walkthrough.article.tab.message: A tab on the right edge of the window opens the Meta Report: everything ORE found, in one place. Drag it up or down if it covers something.

walkthrough.article.title.message: On an article page, two things appear

walkthrough.article.turnOff.text.message: Click the ORE button in your browser toolbar to hide it on this page, snooze it on this site, or turn it off for the site entirely.

walkthrough.article.turnOff.title.message: Turn it off where you don't want it

walkthrough.demo.scanning.message: ORE is looking up the papers on this page…

walkthrough.done.text.message: Setup is complete. Start using the plugin: ORE will check papers by itself as you browse.

walkthrough.dots.article.message: The pill and the side tab

walkthrough.notices.local.text.message: ORE keeps its own copy of the retraction list and refreshes it weekly, so no server learns what you are reading.

walkthrough.notices.meaning.message: A retraction means the paper has been withdrawn, usually because of serious errors or misconduct. An expression of concern means the journal has flagged a problem that is not yet resolved; the paper still stands.

walkthrough.notices.where.message: Either one adds a warning to the end of the pill and appears in the Meta Report. Both link to the journal's notice, so you can read the reason. The data comes from Retraction Watch.

walkthrough.pill.board.closedText.message: Everything found for this paper, at a glance

walkthrough.pill.board.nothingText.message: All faded: open it to check every lookup finished

walkthrough.pill.board.openText.message: One row per part, each a link or an action

walkthrough.pill.doi.text.message: Copy the DOI or a formatted reference, or open the paper. A dotted underline means it was matched by title.

walkthrough.pill.oa.text.message: Open Access: a legal open-access version is online, found through Unpaywall. The row opens the best version; the arrow beside it lists the others.

walkthrough.pill.open.message: Point at the pill to open it. Each part becomes a row with a link or action. Click to keep it open.

walkthrough.pill.parts.message: Each part of the pill answers one question. A coloured part means yes. A faded part means nothing was found yet, or the check could not be done; open the pill to see which.

walkthrough.pill.pubpeer.text.message: PubPeer is a site where researchers comment on published papers, often to point out problems. The number is the comment count; the row opens the thread.

walkthrough.pill.reps.text.message: A replication repeats the study with new data; a reproduction reruns the original analysis. The number counts replications, or reproductions when there are none; the row shows them in the FLoRA Replication Atlas.

walkthrough.ready.automatic.message: ORE works by itself as you browse. While it checks a page, a small note shows in the corner, then goes away.

walkthrough.ready.later.message: Later, click the ORE toolbar button and choose “Tour this page” for a tour of the page you are on, “How it works” to see this again, or “Settings” to block a site.

walkthrough.ready.sampleError.message: Couldn't open the sample article. Please try again.

walkthrough.ready.toolbar.message: The ORE button in your browser toolbar shows a number when papers on the page have something to report. Click it to pause or turn off ORE on a site.

walkthrough.ready.tryText.message: See ORE on a real paper, with a short guided tour.

walkthrough.report.atlas.text.message: A free database, run by the FORRT community, of studies in the social and behavioural sciences that repeated earlier findings, and what they found. Every replication count in ORE comes from it and links to the evidence.

walkthrough.report.atlas.title.message: What the FLoRA Replication Atlas is

walkthrough.report.caution.message: Treat outcome labels as a starting point, not a verdict on the original. They depend on how replication authors describe their results. A failed replication does not by itself show that the original finding was false or the original study flawed: a replication can also fail by chance, because of low power or problems in its own conduct, or because conditions, situations, or contexts differed.

walkthrough.report.contents.message: The side tab opens a report on the article you are reading: its replications and what they found, any retraction or concern, its PubPeer discussion, and which of its references have something to report.

walkthrough.report.original.message: If the article is itself a replication, the report shows the original study it repeated.

walkthrough.report.share.text.message: Print makes a printable page. Copy link shares the whole report in the link itself, so nothing is uploaded.

walkthrough.report.title.message: The Meta Report: everything in one place

walkthrough.search.copy.text.message: The quote icon copies the reference in your chosen citation style, formatting included, ready to paste into Word or Google Docs.

walkthrough.search.dotted.text.message: Two papers can have almost the same title. If the match is wrong, everything else in the panel describes the wrong paper. Open the DOI once to confirm.

walkthrough.search.dotted.title.message: Check a dotted DOI before you rely on it

walkthrough.search.panel.message: On search sites, ORE adds a small panel beside each result to help you skim the results. Click a row to open the paper, copy its reference, find an open-access version, read the discussion, or see its replications. A row that says “Checking…” is still running; it does not mean nothing was found.

walkthrough.search.title.message: Judge a result before you open it

walkthrough.search.titleMatch.message: When a result doesn't show a DOI, ORE looks the title up in Crossref and OpenAlex and picks the closest match by author and year. A DOI found this way is underlined with dots.

walkthrough.setup.citation.help.message: The format the copy button uses: APA, Vancouver, BibTeX and eight more.

walkthrough.setup.citation.saved.context: {style} is a citation style name such as "APA" or "Vancouver"

walkthrough.setup.email.help.message: Needed to find open-access versions: Unpaywall asks for a contact address. ORE also gives it to Crossref, OpenAlex and NCBI when it looks papers up. Remove it any time.

walkthrough.setup.email.invalid.message: That doesn't look like an email address.

walkthrough.setup.email.removed.message: Email removed. Title matching and open-access lookups need an email; other checks still work.

walkthrough.setup.email.saved.message: Email saved. Reload open tabs to use it for lookups.

walkthrough.setup.intro.message: Your choices are saved as soon as you make them, and you can change them any time in Settings.

walkthrough.setup.sites.intro.message: ORE is on for journals, publishers, preprint servers and documents, and off for shopping, video, messaging and web search. Tick or untick a category, or open it to choose site by site.

walkthrough.sheets.check.message: Open a spreadsheet of DOIs, such as a reading list or the studies for a review, in Google Sheets or Excel Online. ORE checks every DOI in it, including rows you have not scrolled to, and reports in a popup.

walkthrough.sheets.docs.text.message: Each reference with a DOI gets a small marker. Open it for the same details as a pill.

walkthrough.sheets.docs.title.message: Writing in Google Docs or Word Online?

walkthrough.sheets.hide.text.message: Hide for this sheet closes the card for this sheet. Snooze hides it for ten minutes.

walkthrough.sheets.retracted.message: Retracted papers are listed first, each with a link to its notice, and the popup appears for them even if nothing else was found.

walkthrough.sheets.tabs.text.message: Each sheet tab is checked on its own. Closing the popup on one tab leaves the others alone.

walkthrough.sheets.title.message: Check a whole list of papers at once

walkthrough.stepCount.context: progress label on each walkthrough screen, e.g. "3 of 9"

walkthrough.welcome.articles.text.message: The article, every paper in its reference list, and any DOI mentioned elsewhere on a page.

walkthrough.welcome.doi.message: ORE recognises a paper by its DOI — the permanent ID printed on most research papers, such as 10.1177/0956797610383437. It works in three places.

walkthrough.welcome.footnote.message: What ORE shows is a starting point for your own judgement, not a verdict on a paper.

walkthrough.welcome.intro.message: ORE checks each paper on a page for replications, retractions, PubPeer discussion and open-access versions.

walkthrough.welcome.search.text.message: Google Scholar, PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Scopus and EBSCO: each result gets a panel.

walkthrough.welcome.sheets.text.message: A list of DOIs in Google Sheets or Excel Online, checked in full. References in Google Docs and Word Online are marked as you write.

walkthrough.welcome.title.message: See what is known about a paper while you read
